b: Unthankful leaders turn good into poison.
Ingratitude makes success feel like failure. Generosity becomes duty. Effort becomes drudgery.
People who feel unappreciated eventually wonder why they bother.
Focus on what’s lacking instead of celebrating what went right.
When sales increase 15%, say, “We should have hit 20%.”
Make sure nothing is ever good enough.
Respond to ideas with criticism, complaints, or indifference.
Eventually, people stop bringing their best.
Constantly remind people how much you do for them.
Ask, “Is this the thanks I get for all I’ve done for you?”
Complain about people who aren’t in the room.
An unthankful heart leads people into misery.
Take people for granted. Focus on what annoys you.
Forget consistency and dependability. Drill down on one screw up.
Make people feel like burdens instead of blessings.
Expect yesterday’s favor to be today’s responsibility.
Someone stays late to help you meet a deadline. Assume they’ll stay late every time.
Make people feel obligated to give more. Ignore what they’ve given.
Ingratitude makes people feel used instead of valued.
Ungrateful leaders make themselves miserable. And they pour misery on others.
What’s it like to be on the receiving end of ungrateful leadership?
